requested: 2026-10-31, after specifying the first theory retry
question: Are the apparent failures chiefly instability of small models?
small_data_control: P=17, K=1, W=512, D=1, all three seeds
fixed: Schedule-Free AdamW only, as subsequently requested before these runs started: lr=.003, betas=(.9,.98), decay=1; 10-step external warmup, no built-in warmup or rate decay; 50% train; batch 512; 5000 updates; evaluate complete splits every 250 steps with averaged weights
matched_small_controls: Repeat the three original Schedule-Free aliasing controls at lr=.003 on seeds 17 and 23, supplementing the completed seed 11. Add W64/D1 on P17/K1 at all three seeds. All nine added controls use Schedule-Free AdamW.
measurements: standard deviation of heldout accuracy at steps 3500 through 5000
range and standard deviation of final accuracy over three seeds
character-alias diagnostic and actual readout margins
interpretation: Improvement with size and smaller temporal/seed fluctuations supports the small-model instability explanation in these cases. Persistent poor heldout accuracy with high training accuracy is memorization; low accuracy on both splits is fitting failure. Neither result alone identifies the cause or proves impossibility.
prospective: All definitions and metrics were written before any large-* run was started. The initial smaller-model results motivated this comparison.
